## Quick start

```bash
theme={\"theme\":\"css-variables\"}\n# One command does everything: probe, connect, sweep tools/resources/prompts\nmcpjam server

doctor --url https://your-server.com/mcp
```

If the server requires OAuth, doctor reports `oauth_required` with the discovery
metadata. See [OAuth login](https://docs.mcpjam.com/cli/oauth-login.md) to obtain a token, then re-run with `--oauth-access-token`

.

## Commands

### `server probe`

Stateless HTTP probe; no full client connection. Tests transport selection, OAuth discov

.com/mcp
```

Use this when you want to check reachability and OAuth metadata without triggering a full MCP initialize handshak

e. The probe sends an unauthenticated `initialize` request and inspects the response.

**What it returns:**

* Transport type
(streamable-http, SSE, or failed)\n* OAuth metadata (resource metadata URL, authorization server metadata, registration strategies

, scopes)
* `WWW-Authenticate` header parsing

Credential header values never appear in the printed result. `Authorization`, `C
ookie` and `X-Api-Key` print as `[REDACTED]`. `X-Auth-Token` and other sensitive header names print the first four and last two ch

aracters o

### `server doctor`

Combined triage, runs probe, then attempts a full client connection, then sweeps tools, resou

dable summary
mcpjam server doctor --url https://your-server.com/mcp

# Full JSON artifact with RPC logs
mcpjam server doctor

--url https://your-server.com/mcp --rpc --out doctor.json

# Stdio server
mcpjam server doctor --command node --args server.js

--cwd /path/to/project
```

**What it returns:**

* `status`: `ready`, `oauth_required`, or `error`
* Probe results (transpo

rt, OAuth discovery)
* Initialization info and negotiated capabilities
* Counts: tools, resources, resource templates, prompts
\nFrom a run without credentials, `ready` means the server let MCPJam connect and list without a token. It does not mean every too
l is public: a server can still ask for sign-in when a protected tool is called. To check, c\n\nThe `--out <path>` flag writes the
full JSON artifact to a file, useful for handoff to another engineer or agent.\nFor stdio targets, those artifacts only record th

e explicit env keys you passed
via `-e/--env`; inherited shell variables are not enumerated.

Credential headers (`Authorizatio
n`, `X-Api-Key`, `X-Auth-Token`, and any other sensitive header names) are automatically redacted to `[REDACTED]` in all printed o

utput and written artifacts, including RPC logs attached 

### `server info`

Get initialization info for a connected server.\

n
```bash theme={"theme":"css-variables"}
mcpjam server info --url https://your-server.com/mcp --access-token $TOKEN
```
\
nReturns the server's `serverInfo` (name, version) and `capabilities` from the MCP initialize response.\n\n### `server capabilitie

s`

Get resolved server capabilities.

```bash theme={"theme":"css-variables"}
mcpjam server capabilities --url https://y

our-server.com/mcp --access-token $TOKEN
```

### `server validate`

Connect to a server and verify the debugger surface work

n```

### `server ping`

Simple connectivity check.

```bash theme={"theme":"css-variables"}
mcpjam server ping --url h

ttps://your-server.com/mcp
```

### `server export`

Export a full snapshot of the server's tools, resources, prompts, and ca

s-token $TOKEN > snapshot.json
```

## Shared server flags

Every `server` subcommand accepts these flags for specifying how

to connect:

| Flag | Description |
| - | - |
| `--transport <transport>` | Explicit transport type (`http` or `stdio`) |
| `
--url <url>` | HTTP MCP server URL |\n| `--access-token <token>` | Bearer access token |\n| `--oauth-access-token <token>` | OAuth
bearer access token |\n| `--refresh-token <token>` | OAuth refresh token |\n| `--client-id <id>` | OAuth client ID (used with `--
refresh-token`) |\n| `--client-secret <secret>` | OAuth client secret (used with `--refresh-token`) |\n| `--credentials-file <path
>` | Load OAuth credentials from a file created by `oauth login --credentials-out` or `oauth conformance --credentials-out` |\n| `
--header <header>` | HTTP header in `Key: Value` format (repeatable) |\n| `--client-capabilities <json>` | Client capabilities as
inline JSON, `@path`, or `-` for stdin |\n| `--command <command>` | Command for a stdio server |\n| `--args <arg...>` | Preferred
stdio command arguments |\n| `--command-args <arg>` | Legacy stdio command argument (repeatable) |\n| `-e, --env <env...>` | Stdio

environment `KEY=[REDACTED] values |
| `--cwd <path>` | Working directory for the stdio child process |

Stdio child processes
inherit the parent shell environment by default. Use\n`-e/--env` to add values or override inherited ones, and `--cwd` when the\n
command must run from a project directory.\nIf you pass `--transport`, the CLI validates that it matches the target flags\nyou pro

vided instead of silently inferring the transport.

## Common patterns

### Triage an unknown server

```bash theme={"theme

":"css-variables"}
# Start with doctor
mcpjam server doctor --url https://unknown-server.com/mcp

# If it returns oauth_req
uired, login first\nmcpjam oauth login --url https://unknown-server.com/mcp \\\n --protocol-version 2025-11-25 --registration dcr

ile to discover all available pages before exploring further.

# Local Evals

> Run an MCPJam eval suite file on your machine
with mcpjam test with local results and an MCPJam identity\n\n`mcpjam test <file>` runs an MCPJam suite file locally: it connects
your MCP servers, drives each case's prompts through a model, grades the transcript with the same assertions a hosted run uses, an
d decides the run with\n\nResults are **never uploaded**. The command writes results to your terminal and, if you ask, to a report
file. It records the run start with MCPJam. Like every command, it sends the CLI's single anonymous [telemetry](htt\n\n## Eval id
entity and local data\n\nRun `mcpjam cloud login` locally, or set `MCPJAM_API_KEY` to an organization `sk_` key in CI. The SDK als
o accepts `apiKey` or `mcpjamAuth` in run options. Explicit credentials take precedence over `MCPJAM_API_KEY`, whic\n\nEvery logic
al run needs an online start response. MCPJam retries transient failures within ten seconds, then stops before execution. A prior
successful run does not enable offline execution. The CLI resolves the project \n\nWith results uploads disabled, the start-run re
quest sends only the credential in the authorization header, any MCPJam API headers you configure through the SDK's `inference.res
olveMcpjam`, project selection, a new run-s\n\n`DO_NOT_TRACK`, `MCPJAM_TELEMETRY_DISABLED`, and CLI telemetry settings disable ana
lytics, not the required run-start request. Results remain local unless result uploading is enabled separately.\n\n## Quick start\

n
### 1. Write a suite

Save this as `.mcpjam/evals/example.yaml`:

```yaml theme={"theme":"css-variables"}
schemaVersio

n: "2"
mode: agentWorkflow
reportingMode: standard
suite:
 id: s_notes_example
 name: Notes server
target:
 servers:

- name: notes
defaults:
 judge:
 enabled: false
 model: anthropic/claude-haiku-4.5
 iterations: 1
 passThreshold:

1
 validity: {}
cases:
 - id: c_reads_a_note
 title: reads the note it was asked about
 steps:
 - id: s1

kind: prompt
 prompt: What does note 7 say?
 - id: a1
 kind: assert
 assertion:
 type:

toolCalledAtLeastOnce
 toolName: read_note
 - id: c_never_deletes
 title: never deletes when only asked to read
